pr_title: Setting the sudo_password to fix the sudo_missing_terminal error for latest versions of EL8
pr_body:
## Description
`sudo_password` is set to nil while making a ssh connection on knife bootstrap execution which leads to sudo_missing_terminal error in the latest versions of EL8.
We are setting this sudo_password with the password given when its prompted in terminal and than make a call to train gem for ssh connection which makes a successful Knife bootstrap execution without exposing their admin password in shell

## Related Issue
fixed:  #13271

believe this is fixed in Knife 18 due to the newer Net::SSH, @Stromweld was able to do this successfully against latest EL8 and EL9 from Chef WS 18 without any such fixes. > > So this is probably only broken in 17, where this code won't go. Can you repro the bug with Knife 18? > > If not, I suggest instead of this we just backport the newer Net::SSH in 17 (there's already a PR for it, but the build pipelines are still broken). > > That make sense? > > (speaking on behalf of @tpowell-progress , myself, and @Stromweld ) As mentioned this error was coming in knife: 17 which includes net-ssh 7.0.1 and I was successfully able to replicate this error. But I tried this whole setup with Knife 18 also which includes updated net-ssh 7.1.0 and still facing the same error. Please find below screenshots, If I use -P option with password here as mentioned in the error and execute the command then it works fine without failure (with both the setup knife 17 and Knife 18). I also discussed with @Stromweld and we have to use -P and pass the password as it’s running under ruby and thus ruby needs to pass in the password. And If there is a ask for password prompt then it would be a bit of work to add a password prompt. That would then be a feature request Hi, I tried this whole setup with redhat v7.9(where the bootstrap succeeds) and redhat v9.0(where the bootstrap failing) with/without using -P password option here. Below are my analysis. When we run bootstrap with -P "password" option, it succeeds with both the redhat versions because we pass connection_password(-P option) which gets assign to sudo_password key (https://github.com/chef/chef/blob/main/knife/lib/chef/knife/bootstrap.rb#L1028) and then makes a call to train-core gem. Without -P "password" option it succeeds for the version 7.9 and failed for the version 9.0 because of below reason - For v7.9 - While execution it prompt for the password and assign that given password to the password key and the sudo_password key is nil, It failed for the first time with the warning `"sudo: 1 incorrect password attempt"` and ask for the sudo password again and now it assign that password to the `sudo_password` key while making a call to train-core gem(which in place do a ssh call or establish ssh connection) again and this time the call succeeds. ref - https://github.com/chef/chef/blob/main/knife/lib/chef/knife/bootstrap.rb#L710 ![image](https://github.com/chef/chef/assets/35272911/79e4565b-5378-4b82-a6af-45eff40571bc) For v9.0 While execution it prompt for the password and assign that given password to the password key and the sudo_password key is nil. It failed with the `"ERROR: Sudo password is required for this operation. Please enter password using -P or --ssh-password option."` and it dosen't prompt for the password 2nd time as it does for version lesser than EL8. So on a call to a train-core gem we get response `":sudo_missing_terminal"` for latest version of EL8 which goes to rescue block where it gets failed with error (ref- https://github.com/chef/chef/blob/main/knife/lib/chef/knife/bootstrap.rb#L709). ![image](https://github.com/chef/chef/assets/35272911/464960d9-01b4-4338-8e09-7a07a3c756f6) So the reason of failure here is `sudo_password` is set to nil and when we make a call for ssh connection as the ruby needs to pass in the password. A tty session would just sit waiting till timeout due to session running in ruby and ruby isn’t prompting for password again or taking input from stdin. If we set this `sudo_password` while making a call it will work, I tried to manually add sudo_password and make a call to train-core gem and it worked > Can you include a screenshot of what this looks like working in RHEL 7.9 and RHEL 9? This screenshot is when we pass connection_password or -P "password" (exposing password in shell) in the command itself for both rhel 7.9 and rhel 9. In this case it wont promt for sudo_pass and we prefer connection_password over sudo_pass here. This screenshot is when we wont pass connection_password or -P "password" in the command for both rhel 7.9 and rhel 9. In this case it will promt for sudo_pass here. So if we have a connection_password present we prefer connection_password over sudo_pass and if connection_password is not passed or nil we will consider the sudo_pass here passed from the prompt. issue_context.title: Set :non_interactive option for Net::SSH to false when RequestTTY is configured in user ssh config file
issue_context.body:
<!---
!!!!!! NOTE: CHEF CLIENT BUGS ONLY !!!!!!

This issue tracker is for the code contained within this repo -- `chef-client`, base `knife` functionality (not
plugins), `chef-apply`, `chef-solo`, `chef-client -z`, etc.

* Requests for new or alternative functionality should be made to [feedback.chef.io](https://feedback.chef.io/forums/301644-chef-product-feedback/category/110832-chef-client)
* [Chef Server issues](https://github.com/chef/chef-server/issues/new)
* [ChefDK issues](https://github.com/chef/chef-dk/issues/new)
* Cookbook Issues (see the https://github.com/chef-cookbooks repos or search [Supermarket](https://supermarket.chef.io) or GitHub/Google)

-->

## Description
<!--- Briefly describe the issue -->
In latest versions of EL8 (CentOS, RedHat, Rocky, etc), OpenSSH sever doesn't privide TTY for connections unless it is requested by SSH client explicitly:

```
$ ssh 10.0.0.2 "sh -c '(sudo echo) < /dev/null'"
Private IP: 10.0.0.2

sudo: a terminal is required to read the password; either use the -S option to read from standard input or configure an askpass helper
```
It causes issue for `knife bootstrap` using `sudo` to failed. Providing password in command line also doesn't help.

For OpenSSH client, we can solve it by add `RequestTTY yes` in `~/.ssh/config`. However, it doesn't work for knife. _RequestTTY_ is not an option which can be parsed by [Net::SSH::Config](https://github.com/net-ssh/net-ssh/blob/master/lib/net/ssh/config.rb#L9). 

We could ask Net::SSH to translate the value of `RequestTTY` to `non_interactive`. However, they are not meant to the same option. Could you add pieces of code for knife to set the SSH connection option `:non_interactive` to `false` when _RequestTTY_ is set `yes`?

## Chef Version
<!--- Tell us which version of chef-client you are using (see below for Server+ChefDK bugs). -->
knife: 17.10.0 (from Chef-Workstation)

## Platform Version
<!--- Tell us which operating system distribution and version chef-client is running on. -->
CentOS/Rocky Linux release 8.6

## Replication Case
<!--- Tell us what steps to take to replicate your problem.  See [How to create a Minimal, Complete, and Verifiable example](https://stackoverflow.com/help/mcve)
for information on how to create a good replication case. -->
Follow the steps to reproduce:
- Create a latest CentOS/Rocky 8 server. Create a normal user on it and grant sudo access. Password is required for sudo. Here is the sample sudoer config:
  ```
  myuser ALL=(ALL) ALL
  ```
- Try to bootstrap it with knife:
  ```bash
  knife bootstrap "10.0.0.2" --node-name "my_chef_node" --connection-user "myuser" --sudo --use-sudo-password
  ```
## Client Output
<!--- The relevant output of the chef-client run or a link to a gist of the entire run, if there is one.

The debug output (chef-client -l debug) may be useful, but please link to a gist, or truncate it. -->

```
$ knife bootstrap "10.0.0.2" --node-name "my_chef_node" --connection-user "myuser" --sudo --use-sudo-password
Connecting to 10.0.0.2 using ssh
ERROR: Sudo password is required for this operation. Please enter password using -P or --ssh-password option
Creating new client for my_chef_node
Creating new node for my_chef_node
ERROR: Train::UserError: Sudo failed: Sudo cannot prompt for password because there is no terminal. Please provide the sudo password directly
$
$ knife bootstrap "10.0.0.2" --node-name "my_chef_node" --connection-user "myuser" --sudo --use-sudo-password -P "mypassword"
Connecting to 10.0.0.2 using ssh
WARN: [SSH] connection failed, terminating (#<Net::SSH::AuthenticationFailed: Authentication failed for user myuser@10.0.0.2>)
ERROR: Train::Transports::SSHFailed: SSH session could not be established
```

review_comments: should this be the other way? If someone explicitly passed in `sudo_pass`, shouldn't we use that instead of the connection_password?

So connection_password will always take precedence over the sudo_pass if  connection_password is passed. sudo_pass will be passed during the promt only and if connection_password or -P is passed the prompt will not come and connection_password will take precedence.
If connection_password or -P is not passed then only the terminal will be prompted for sudo_pass.
So ,  sudo_pass will be passed during prompt only and we will use that instead of the connection_password
